searchText: Retesteth doesn't generate the state. An evm implementation required. That's the point we came up to 3 years ago. So that any client can be used to generate the tests. Retesteth is like hive in this matter I am not quite understand what kind of documentation you want? <@211091239112671234> is there more documentation on t8ntool? If you need more documentation on t8ntool we can write No I don't get the problem with the doc license Would it be better if I submit the CLI spec as an EIP? The problem with EIP is that it's more difficult to evolve the spec, going forward We could add it to the Eth-1.0 specs repo Seems like it could fit there under the right license? https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs We could make a folder for it and give it a home. Either an EIP or not part of a GPL licensed code repo. Not just the CLI but documentation for the file formats too. Ok, maybe the specs repo then. I'll try to get it written, however, I have some work ahead of me first to get it to accept acl-transactions Also, a cross-client standard being homed in one clients repo isn't a good look. ehtereum/tests would also be a good home. Yes tests might be best I still haven't written a good spec, but what I have done, is update the PR (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/21502) . Specifically, the `evm t8n` tool. cc <@!393119312350543872> example usage is here: https://github.com/lightclient/go-ethereum/tree/impl-eip-2718/cmd/evm/testdata/8 . The two new features added are 1) that it supports ACL-transactions, and 2) that it supports signing, so that it can use `secretKey` to sign a tx (it requires v,r,s to be all zero in that case). So now it would be possible to generate official reference tests with access lists

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
I still haven't written a good spec, but what I have done, is update the PR (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/21502) . Specifically, the `evm t8n` tool. cc <@!393119312350543872> example usage is here: https://github.com/lightclient/go-ethereum/tree/impl-eip-2718/cmd/evm/testdata/8 . 

The two new features added are 1) that it supports ACL-transactions, and 2) that it supports signing, so that it can use `secretKey` to sign a tx (it requires v,r,s to be all zero in that case).
